body.en: Advanced Algebra forms approximately 20% of the EST II Math Level 1 subject test. The examination tests higher-level algebraic capabilities beyond EST I: rational expressions and algebraic fractions with domain restrictions, polynomial long division and synthetic division, application of the Remainder and Factor Theorems, solving nonlinear systems (lines intersecting parabolas or circles), and eliminating extraneous solutions introduced by clearing algebraic denominators.

label.en: Definition 1.1 — Rational Functions, Polynomial Division, and Conjugate Roots

body.en:
Core algebraic concepts and structural theorems for polynomial and rational functions:
  • Rational Functions & Domain Restrictions: A rational function has form \(R(x) = \frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\) where \(P(x)\) and \(Q(x)\) are polynomials. The natural domain comprises all real numbers such that \(Q(x) \neq 0\).
    1. Vertical Asymptotes: Occur at zeros of \(Q(x)\) that are not zeros of \(P(x)\).
    2. Removable Discontinuities (Holes): Occur when a factor \((x - c)\) cancels from both \(P(x)\) and \(Q(x)\).
  • Polynomial Division Algorithm: For any polynomial \(P(x)\) and non-zero divisor \(D(x)\), there exist unique polynomials \(Q(x)\) (quotient) and \(R(x)\) (remainder) such that:
    \[ P(x) = D(x) \cdot Q(x) + R(x) \]
    where either \(R(x) = 0\) or \(\deg(R) < \deg(D)\). When dividing by a linear factor \(D(x) = x - c\), the remainder is a constant \(R\).
  • Complex Conjugate Root Theorem: If a polynomial \(P(x)\) has real coefficients and \(a + bi\) is a root (\(b \neq 0\)), then its complex conjugate \(a - bi\) is also guaranteed to be a root.
  • Absolute Value Compound Inequalities:
    1. \(|f(x)| \le c \iff -c \le f(x) \le c\) (conjunction, bounded interval).
    2. \(|f(x)| \ge c \iff f(x) \le -c \quad \text{or} \quad f(x) \ge c\) (disjunction, union of rays).

label.en: Theorem 1.1 — Remainder & Factor Theorems, Rational Root Theorem, and Nonlinear Systems

body.en:
Analytical theorems for polynomial manipulation and system solutions:
  • Polynomial Remainder Theorem: When a polynomial \(P(x)\) is divided by the linear binomial \((x - c)\), the numerical remainder is \(R = P(c)\). If dividing by \((ax - b)\), the remainder is \(R = P\left(\frac{b}{a}\right)\).
  • Factor Theorem: A linear polynomial \((x - c)\) is a factor of \(P(x) \iff P(c) = 0\). Consequently, \(x = c\) is a root of the equation \(P(x) = 0\).
  • Rational Root Theorem: For a polynomial with integer coefficients \(P(x) = a_n x^n + \dots + a_1 x + a_0\) (\(a_n, a_0 \neq 0\)), every rational root \(\frac{p}{q}\) in lowest terms satisfies: \(p\) is a factor of constant term \(a_0\), and \(q\) is a factor of leading coefficient \(a_n\).
  • Nonlinear Systems Consistency: When solving a system composed of a quadratic curve \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) and a linear equation \(y = mx + k\), equating expressions yields the quadratic: \(ax^2 + (b - m)x + (c - k) = 0\).
    1. \(\Delta > 0\): The line cuts the curve at two distinct points (secant line).
    2. \(\Delta = 0\): The line touches the curve at exactly one point (tangent line).
    3. \(\Delta < 0\): The line and curve have no real points of intersection.

label.en: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Rational Equations & Polynomial Theorems

body.en:
• Extraneous Solutions in Rational Equations: When multiplying across by the LCD, you may introduce solutions that make an original denominator zero. Always substitute candidate solutions back into the original denominators to verify they are non-zero.
  • Remainder Theorem Sign Inversion: When dividing \(P(x)\) by \((x - c)\), the remainder is \(P(c)\). But when dividing by \((x + c)\), the divisor is \((x - (-c))\), so the remainder is \(P(-c)\). Misplacing this minus sign is the #1 error on EST II polynomial questions.
  • Absolute Value Inequalities: \(|x - a| \le b\) translates to the compound inequality \(-b \le x - a \le b\) (an intersection/interval). In contrast, \(|x - a| \ge b\) translates to \(x - a \le -b\) OR \(x - a \ge b\) (a union of disjoint rays).
  • Nonlinear Systems Intersection Count: When solving a system of a parabola \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) and line \(y = mx + k\), substitute to obtain a single quadratic. Check the discriminant \(\Delta = B^2 - 4AC\): \(\Delta > 0\) gives 2 real solutions, \(\Delta = 0\) gives 1 tangent point, and \(\Delta < 0\) gives no real intersections.

label.en: Worked Example 1.A — Rational Expression Simplification & Restrictions

body.en:
Simplify the rational expression \(\dfrac{2x^2 - 7x - 4}{x^2 - 16}\) and identify all excluded domain values.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor the numerator: Find factors of \(a \cdot c = 2(-4) = -8\) summing to \(-7\), which are \(-8\) and \(+1\):
    \[ 2x^2 - 8x + x - 4 = 2x(x - 4) + 1(x - 4) = (2x + 1)(x - 4) \]
  2. Factor the denominator (difference of squares):
    \[ x^2 - 16 = (x - 4)(x + 4) \]
  3. State domain restrictions: Denominators cannot be zero:
    \[ (x - 4)(x + 4) eq 0 \implies x eq 4 \quad ext{and} \quad x eq -4 \]
  4. Cancel common factor \((x - 4)\):
    \[ rac{(2x + 1)(x - 4)}{(x - 4)(x + 4)} = \mathbf{ rac{2x + 1}{x + 4}} \quad (x eq 4, -4) \]

label.en: Worked Example 1.B — Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Detection

body.en:
Solve the rational equation \(\dfrac{x}{x - 2} + \dfrac{1}{x + 2} = \dfrac{8}{x^2 - 4}\) for all valid real solutions.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Identify the LCD and restricted values:
    Notice that \(x^2 - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2)\). The least common denominator is \((x - 2)(x + 2)\).
    Restrictions: \(x \neq 2\) and \(x \neq -2\).
  2. Multiply both sides by the LCD:
    \[ x(x + 2) + 1(x - 2) = 8 \]
  3. Expand and collect like terms:
    \[ x^2 + 2x + x - 2 = 8 \implies x^2 + 3x - 10 = 0 \]
  4. Factor the resulting quadratic:
    \[ (x + 5)(x - 2) = 0 \implies x = -5 \quad \text{or} \quad x = 2 \]
  5. Check candidate roots against domain restrictions:
    Candidate \(x = 2\) makes the original denominator \(x - 2 = 0\), so \(x = 2\) is an extraneous solution.
    Candidate \(x = -5\) is valid: \(\frac{-5}{-7} + \frac{1}{-3} = \frac{5}{7} - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{15 - 7}{21} = \frac{8}{21}\), and \(\frac{8}{25 - 4} = \frac{8}{21}\) ✓.
The only valid real solution is \(\mathbf{x = -5}\).

label.en: Worked Example 1.C — Nonlinear System Intersection & Tangency Criterion

body.en:
For what value of the constant \(k\) is the line \(y = 2x + k\) tangent to the parabola \(y = x^2 - 4x + 7\)?

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Equate the line and parabola equations:
    \[ x^2 - 4x + 7 = 2x + k \]
  2. Rearrange into standard quadratic form:
    \[ x^2 - 6x + (7 - k) = 0 \]
  3. Apply the tangency condition (\(\Delta = 0\)):
    A line is tangent to a parabola when they intersect at exactly one point (discriminant must be zero):
    \[ \Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (-6)^2 - 4(1)(7 - k) = 0 \]
    \[ 36 - 28 + 4k = 0 \implies 8 + 4k = 0 \implies 4k = -8 \implies \mathbf{k = -2} \]
  4. Find the point of tangency:
    With \(k = -2\), the quadratic becomes \(x^2 - 6x + 9 = 0 \implies (x - 3)^2 = 0 \implies x = 3\).
    \(y = 2(3) + (-2) = 4\). The unique point of tangency is \((3, 4)\).

label.en: Worked Example D — Algebraic Structure & Vieta's Root Relations

body.en:
Solve the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 10x + 25 = 0 \) and verify the sum and product of its roots.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor into binomials: \( (x - 5)(x - 5) = 0 \implies x = 5 \text{ or } x = 5 \).
  2. Check Vieta's formulas: sum \( = 5 + 5 = \mathbf{10} \) and product \( = (5)(5) = \mathbf{25} \).

solution.en:
Step 1: Apply quotient law of logarithms: \[ \log_2\left(\frac{x + 4}{x}\right) = 3 \]

Step 2: Convert to exponential form: \[ \frac{x + 4}{x} = 2^3 = 8 \]

Step 3: Solve for \(x\): \[ x + 4 = 8x \implies 7x = 4 \implies \mathbf{x = \frac{4}{7}}. \]

Step 4: Check domain: For \(x = 4/7\), both \(x > 0\) and \(x + 4 > 0\) are strictly positive ✓.

question.en: Solve the nonlinear system of equations: \[ \begin{cases} y = x^2 - 4x + 3 \\ 2x + y = 6 \end{cases} \] Find all points of intersection \((x, y)\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Isolate \(y\) from the linear equation: \[ y = 6 - 2x \]

Step 2: Substitute into the quadratic equation: \[ 6 - 2x = x^2 - 4x + 3 \implies x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0. \]

Step 3: Factor the quadratic: \[ (x - 3)(x + 1) = 0 \implies x_1 = 3, \quad x_2 = -1. \]

Step 4: Compute corresponding \(y\)-values:

  • For \(x = 3\): \(y = 6 - 2(3) = 0 \implies \mathbf{(3, 0)}\).
  • For \(x = -1\): \(y = 6 - 2(-1) = 8 \implies \mathbf{(-1, 8)}\).

The points of intersection are \(\mathbf{(3, 0)}\) and \(\mathbf{(-1, 8)}\).

question.en: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^3 - kx^2 + 5x - 7\) is divided by \((x - 2)\), the remainder is \(11\). Find the value of \(k\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Apply the Remainder Theorem: The remainder when dividing by \((x - 2)\) is \(P(2)\): \[ P(2) = 11 \]

Step 2: Evaluate \(P(2)\): \[ P(2) = 2(2^3) - k(2^2) + 5(2) - 7 = 2(8) - 4k + 10 - 7 = 16 - 4k + 3 = 19 - 4k \]

Step 3: Equate and solve for \(k\): \[ 19 - 4k = 11 \implies 4k = 19 - 11 = 8 \implies \mathbf{k = 2}. \]

The value of \(k\) is \(\mathbf{2}\).

question.en: Find all real solutions to the rational equation \(\dfrac{2}{x - 3} - \dfrac{3}{x + 1} = \dfrac{8}{x^2 - 2x - 3}\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Factor denominators: \(x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x - 3)(x + 1)\). LCD is \((x - 3)(x + 1)\). Restrictions: \(x \neq 3, -1\).

Step 2: Multiply through by LCD: \[ 2(x + 1) - 3(x - 3) = 8 \implies 2x + 2 - 3x + 9 = 8 \implies -x + 11 = 8 \implies -x = -3 \implies x = 3. \]

Step 3: Check restriction: \(x = 3\) is a restricted value causing division by zero in the original equation.

Therefore, \(x = 3\) is extraneous and the equation has no solution (empty set \(\emptyset\)).
